title: Run a load test in the Test Builder

blocks.content: See how a website or API holds up under traffic before your users find out. You'll build a performance test in a visual editor, run it from Grafana Cloud, and read the results. Nothing to install, no script to write.
First, open the Test Builder. You need the **Editor** or **Admin** role in your stack.
Click **Testing & synthetics** in the main menu.
Click **Performance**.
Click **Create test**.
Choose **HTTP API**. That's the kind of test the Test Builder creates.
Skip the main options. For the no-code path, click **Try the Test Builder** at the bottom.
The Test Builder is open. It's a visual editor that writes the test script for you.
Now build the test and run it.
Name the test so you can find it again later.
Click **Request** to add an HTTP request, the thing your test will do over and over.

Enter the URL to test. `https://quickpizza.grafana.com` is Grafana's demo site, and you have permission to load test it. Only ever test endpoints you own or have permission to test, because the traffic is real.
Review the summary above the builder before you run. It estimates what the run costs in VUh (virtual user hours) and how long it takes.
Click **Create and run**. Grafana Cloud starts sending traffic to the target and opens the results page.
Your test is running from a load generator in the cloud, not your machine.
The results page opened by itself. Here's how to read it.
Review the bar at the top. It tracks the run status, cost in VUh, virtual users, and where the traffic comes from.
Watch the results stream in while the test runs. You can see how many requests are being sent, how fast the target answers, and whether any fail.
Check Cloud Insights when the run finishes. It scores the run against best practices and flags problems automatically.
Click **ANALYSIS** to explore every metric the run recorded, when the overview isn't enough.
You ran a real load test and read its results, entirely in Grafana Cloud.

Note: Every run bills VUh, which is virtual users times duration. The builder shows the estimate before you run, so check it before you scale a test up. When you're ready for realistic traffic, shape it in the scenario **Options** with ramp-ups, steady load, or a fixed number of iterations.
